scenes.heading: Powers and roots extended
scenes.sub: Can you find √1764 without a calculator?
scenes.say: Can you find the square root of one thousand seven hundred and sixty-four without a calculator? With prime factors, you can. In this video you will learn the index laws, cube roots, and how to find and estimate roots.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Fold paper 3 times, then 4 more: 7 folds in total
scenes.breaks: Real paper can only be folded about 7 times; an index can be as big as you like.
scenes.say: Fold a sheet of paper in half and you get two layers. Fold again, four layers, then eight. Fold three times, then four more times, and you have folded seven times. So two cubed times two to the four is two to the seven. Counting the folds is easier than counting the layers.
scenes.caption: 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷

scenes.heading: The index laws (same base)
scenes.say: When the bases are the same: multiplying powers, add the indices. Dividing, subtract them. A power of a power, multiply them. And any number, except zero, to the power zero is one.

scenes.heading: Square root by prime factors
scenes.question: Find √1764.
scenes.say: Write one thousand seven hundred and sixty-four as two squared times three squared times seven squared. Every index is even, so it is a perfect square. Halve every index: two times three times seven, which is forty-two.

scenes.heading: Estimating a square root
scenes.question: Between which two whole numbers is √90?
scenes.say: Find the squares either side of ninety. Nine squared is eighty-one and ten squared is one hundred. So the square root of ninety is between nine and ten, about nine point four nine.

scenes.heading: Make a perfect square or cube
scenes.question: 72 = 2³ × 3². Smallest multiplier for a square? For a cube?
scenes.say: Seventy-two is two cubed times three squared. For a perfect square, every index must be even, so multiply by two to get one hundred and forty-four. For a perfect cube, every index must be a multiple of three, so multiply by three to get two hundred and sixteen.

points: Halve every index for a square root
scenes.say: Remember: multiply means add the indices, divide means subtract, and a power of a power means multiply. Anything to the power zero is one. And halve every index to find a square root. Now try the practice questions!
